# `11-execution` — Execution Core

## Purpose

The critical path: order -> risk -> execution -> deal -> position -> ledger, with exactly-once financial effect under retries, crashes and partitions.

## Depends on

- [`10-oms`](10-oms.md) — Order Management System
- [`03-ledger`](03-ledger.md) — Double-Entry Ledger
- [`05-position`](05-position.md) — Position Engine

## Depended on by

- [`12-risk-book`](12-risk-book.md) — Internal Risk Book
- [`15-reconciliation`](15-reconciliation.md) — Reconciliation

## Inputs

- accepted orders
- fills
- quotes

## Outputs

- Deal
- position updates
- ledger postings
- execution reports

## What gets built

- transactional outbox / inbox for exactly-once effects
- deal construction: price, quantity, commission, swap, fees
- atomic commit of deal + position + ledger effects
- compensating actions that are themselves recorded and balanced

## Invariants

These are executed as tests at gate **G4**. A module may not declare an
invariant it does not test.

- INV-100: every execution produces exactly one financial deal.
- INV-101: every deal produces exactly one balanced set of ledger postings.
- INV-102: network retries are safe; financial effects are not repeatable.
- INV-103: no deal exists without an originating order and a recorded risk decision.
- INV-104: a crash at any point leaves the system in a state that replay reproduces exactly.

## Test obligations

- exactly-once under duplicate execution reports
- fault injection at every commit boundary
- process kill, database failure, network partition, clock skew
- replay equivalence after each injected fault
- race: concurrent fills on one position

## Known failure modes

The things that go wrong in systems like this one. Each should map to a test above.

- commission charged twice on a retried execution
- one fill recorded as two deals
